text:
Mira: Heads-up — we're seeing a latency spike and ~12-18% request errors on inference in us-west1-b starting 09:12 UTC. Noticing more preemptions than usual. :rotating_light:
Jordan: oncall pinged. Can you paste the error shape?
Mira: 09:12 logs: `gpu-serve-4` termination notice, then lots of `Failed to allocate KV cache` and timeouts.
Mira: small excerpt: ```
Sep 21 09:12:07 gpu-serve-4 kubelet[...]: Node preempted: Reclaim by provider
Sep 21 09:12:09 inference-svc[worker]: ERROR model-run -- err=KV cache miss + OOM
Sep 21 09:12:14 router: 503 upstream timeout for /v1/generate from pool=spot-usw1-b
```
Devin: looks like a concentrated spot eviction wave in us-west1-b. Cloud console shows surge in preemptible reclaim signals.
Riley: autoscaler reacted but replacement preemptible instances are queued behind quota/spot pricing, so cold-starts are high.
Sam: traffic-wise what % routed to that AZ?
Mira: about 22% of inference traffic for this shard (routing by latency/region).
Alex: two options: (1) route traffic away from us-west1-b to other regions/azs and enable on-demand fallback; (2) increase reserved buffer in that AZ (warm on-demand or reserved instances) to absorb interruptions.
Jordan: short-term mitigation: can we enable regional fallback policy to push requests to us-west1-a and us-west1-c and drop batching thresholds for spot pools?
Devin: on it. I'll flip the routing policy to prefer on-demand for 10m and reduce spot pool concurrency. Command: `rdwctl routing set --region us-west1 --prefer-on-demand 600` (simulated).
ops-bot: routing change applied by Devin at 09:18 UTC — preferring on-demand in us-west1 for 10m.
Mira: initial results: error rate dropped from 16% -> 4% within 90s, p95 latency improved but cost will increase.
Sam: can we also temporarily reduce max_batch for GPU workers in spot pools to lower OOMs?
Devin: yes, lowering `max_batch` from 32 -> 12 on spot pods. Patch rolling now. `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/spot-worker MAX_BATCH=12`
Riley: note: lowering batch increases per-token cost but reduces latency and memory pressure. Good trade for 15-30m.
Alex: long-term: recommend increasing warm on-demand buffer for critical shards to 10% of capacity and add preempt-notice handler to proactively flush KV caches and checkpoint.
Jordan: create an action item for capacity planning and cost impact analysis. @Riley can you own?
Riley: will do. I'll open RFC for warm-buffer + preempt handler and estimate monthly cost delta.
Mira: cloud provider support ticket opened (CS-47219) — they flagged a regional capacity reclaim in us-west1-b between 09:10-09:20 UTC.
Sam: any signs of network instability or is this strictly instance reclaim?
Devin: mostly reclaim signals, but there were a few pod restarts with `NetworkPolicy` denies hitting readiness probes. Investigating whether control plane retries affected endpoints.
Jordan: ok good triage. For now keep routing pref to on-demand and monitor for 30m. If spot availability recovers we can roll back.
Mira: monitoring dashboards: p50/p95/p99 trending down after routing change. Will post update at +30m.
ops-bot: incident created — incident/2024-09-21-spot-usw1-b-partial.json by Jordan at 09:20 UTC.
Alex: quick ask for the incident notes: include exact cost delta estimate for 10m pref-on-demand + reduced batching. I can model impact for forecasting.
Riley: note saved. Also adding a follow-up to evaluate mixed pool sizing algorithm to prefer heterogeneous eviction-resilient placement next rollout.
Mira: thanks all. Will keep watching. :thumbsup:
Jordan: thanks team — nice fast coordination. If anything flares up ping pager.
Mira (09:42): 30m check-in — stable, errors ~<2%, will leave routing pref for another 20m to ensure steady state.
Devin (09:45): rolling back MAX_BATCH after 40m; will keep alert thresholds tight.
Riley (10:05): RFC created: `warm-buffer-preempt-handler.md` and assigned to eng-runtime for review.
